newsitem.title: Netherlands: EU urges restraint in Albania, wants new elections.
newsitem.headline: EU urges restraint in Albania, wants new elections.

text.p: The European Union called on Tuesday for "maximum self-restraint" in Albania and said it believed fresh parliamentary elections and a new constitution were needed in the troubled Balkan nation.
"The EU...condemns all attempts by threat or use of arms to undermine stability or seize power," the Dutch EU presidency said in a statement.
"At the same time, the EU believes a parallel process to promote national reconciliation is necessary, leading to a perspective of fresh parliamentary elections and a new constitution."
A failure of pyramid investment schemes in January sparked widespread anti-government riots and protests which turned into an armed revolt, concentrated in the south of the country.
Albanian President Sali Berisha signed a weekend accord with opposition parties calling for all-party government, elections by June and an amnesty for anyone handing in arms within a week.
The EU said it wanted the opposition to cooperate with the government and it expected the Albanian authorities to respect human rights and fundamental freedoms.
"A state of public emergency should not be used to subvert these rights nor the democratic order and the EU expects it to be lifted as soon as possible," the Dutch statement said.
The Albanian parliament, dominated by Berisha's Democratic Party, declared a state of emergency at the start of the month.
The government also had to do more to defend freedom of expression, the EU said.
"The Albanian authorities are expected to maintain freedom of information and must stop the harassment of foreign and national media organisations."
Albanian human rights groups earlier called for the urgent protection of local journalists after a newspaper reported that death lists were circulating naming a number of them.
Both Britain and the Netherlands on Tuesday urged all their citizens, including journalists, to leave Albania as soon as possible.
Earlier the Strasbourg-based Council of Europe urged Albanians to hand over arms and weapons without delay.

"The Council of Europe joins in the urgent appeal to all Albanians to abandon violence and to hand over arms and weapons without delay, so as to allow the rule of law to prevail and democracy to function," Finnish Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen, who chairs the 40-member Council's committee of ministers, said in a statement.
